Title: Ask HN: What is the most useful thing AI has done for you?
HN text: I had a deep conversation with a friend about what is the most useful thing AI has created/done for either of us. For my private life, AI helped me to diagnose and root caused a running toilet, and avoided the high cost of a plumber. It even help to select the replacement parts and how to replace them. Of course, on the tech side, AI is helping me build a healthcare company. What was yours?

A few months ago I wrote about “good enough” models , arguing that cheap models had gotten smart enough for most coding work, and that the expensive frontier models were best saved for the tasks that actually need them. That’s mostly played out as expected. Which leaves a new question: once you’re sure you don’t need the smartest model for a task, how do you find the cheapest one that’s still smart enough?

Title: Why Math Dumped OpenAI
Description: Honest people cannot "embrace change" when that change is a lie.

Article text:
Why Math Dumped OpenAI Ray Myers
Don’t let anyone call the mathematicians Luddites. No.
AI in Math had a natural synergy that researchers made every effort to embrace. OpenAI turned this into a toxic relationship. This breakdown in trust runs parallel to what we see in Software Engineering and other domains.
When programmers say mathematicians are “feeling our pain” now, some mean it in the sense of being shocked to discover machines have surpassed them. That’s a naive but understandable take if you’ve seen recent headlines without prior knowledge of the situation. I’ll explain.
OpenAI’s position at the frontier of Mathematics is not that of the player making the biggest contribution, but of the player with the highest budget, biggest mouth, and least integrity.
